concepts.title: Factorial Notation and Ratios of Factorials
concepts.definition: The factorial of a whole number multiplies every counting number up to it, with zero factorial fixed at one; a ratio of two factorials cancels the shared tail, leaving only a short product of the leading factors.
concepts.key_idea: Expand only the excess factors on top; the common tail cancels without computing.

solution_steps.explain: the tail of the bigger factorial cancels the smaller one

concepts.title: Rule of Sum for Exclusive Alternatives
concepts.definition: When a job is done through mutually exclusive channels, the total count is the sum of the counts of the separate channels, since no choice can belong to two channels at once.
concepts.key_idea: Either-or means add; check the channels never overlap.

concepts.title: Rule of Product for Successive Choices
concepts.definition: When a job breaks into successive independent stages, each stage multiplies its own count of options onto the running total, because every option of one stage pairs with every option of the next.
concepts.key_idea: Stage after stage means multiply; lock fixed slots to one option first.

concepts.title: Permutations of n Distinct Objects Taken r at a Time
concepts.definition: An arrangement in definite order of r objects chosen from n distinct ones counts as a permutation; filling r slots in turn gives a falling product that stops after r factors.
concepts.key_idea: Each filled slot removes one candidate for the next slot.

concepts.title: Permutations with Repetition Allowed
concepts.definition: When a chosen object may be reused at every slot, each of the r slots keeps the full n options, so the count is n raised to the power r; a restricted first slot simply multiplies by its own smaller option count.
concepts.key_idea: Repetition frees every slot to keep the full choice set.

concepts.title: Arrangements with Repeated Letters
concepts.definition: Arranging all letters of a word where some letters repeat divides the total linear order by the product of factorials of each repetition count, since swapping identical letters creates no new word.
concepts.key_idea: Full factorial on top, one factorial on the bottom per repeated letter type.

concepts.title: Circular Permutations and Necklaces
concepts.definition: Arranging objects around a circle fixes no starting point, so one object anchors the ring and the rest permute, giving one less than the linear count; when mirror images count as one, the answer halves again.
concepts.key_idea: Anchor one seat to kill the rotation, halve for reflections on a garland.

concepts.title: Combinations of n Objects Taken r at a Time
concepts.definition: A combination is a selection where order carries no weight; it equals the permutation count divided by the factorial of the selection size, and each combination expands as a falling product over the rising factorial of r.
concepts.key_idea: Select first, arrange never; divide the permutation count by r factorial.

concepts.title: Committee Selections with At Least Conditions
concepts.definition: An at least requirement splits into exhaustive disjoint cases by exact composition; each case multiplies independent group choices, and the case counts add to the final total.
concepts.key_idea: List every allowed mix, multiply within a case, add across cases.

concepts.title: Counting Lines and Triangles with Collinear Points
concepts.definition: Joining points on a plane counts pairs or triples, but a blocked set of collinear points ruins its own selections: subtract the selections inside the blocked set, and for lines add back the single line they share.
concepts.key_idea: Bad selections collapse; triangles vanish entirely while collinear points still make one line.

concepts.title: Combinations with Repetition
concepts.definition: Selecting r items from n types when each type may repeat as often as needed equals choosing r from a stretched set of size n plus r minus one, since the multiset can be reordered into a standard selection.
concepts.key_idea: Stretch n by r minus one, then take an ordinary combination.

concepts.title: At Least One via Total Minus Excluded
concepts.definition: Counting strings that contain at least one member of a required class subtracts the strings drawn purely from the remaining classes from the unrestricted total, a complement shortcut that avoids casework.
concepts.key_idea: Everything minus the purely forbidden set leaves exactly the required set.
